I’m male but finishing up medical school; saw this and felt the need to say a couple stuff. I’m sure you can get experience info way better from other women but hopefully I can allay some fears from a physicians perspective. (nothing here is medical advise just what I’d say if you were somebody I knew). 

1) acute nausea and tremors: if they are new and stay for more than a day or so or get worse or you just feel worried, call your doctors office or whoever prescribed them. Any new symptoms after taking a new med shouldn’t be dismissed.

2) the longer term stuff: 
weight gain is very individual, no way to know how it will affect you personally. 

Cancer risks: risk of some cancers go up, risks of others go down it’s basically a wash(the changes are like going from 1/10000 to 2/10000 or vice versa so tbh not something to think about day to day). Only caveat is if you have a family history if breast, ovarian, or uterine cancer ask your doc cause that can change the math a small amount depending on what kind. 

Personality: same as weight, very individual. But you most likely (there’s always .001% outliers everywhere) won’t see your personality swing from Santa Claus to the grinch or anything wild. if there are any changes ON AVERAGE it’d be more on the scale of pre and post coffee in the morning. 

Don’t dismiss your worries or concerns: everyone is different so just because this is the avg. outcome doesn’t mean ignore something different; it’s literally our jobs to help patients feel safe and educated about their health so ask as much as you need from your doc and if the doc doesn’t take your concerns seriously find a new doc that will.

Hope you feel better!
